title: Go-to-Prod Signalboard & Adoption Metrics
body:
Purpose
-----
This is a lightweight signalboard intended to guide the last 6 weeks before go-to-prod for feature X (public API throttling + adaptive batching). The focus is two-fold: (1) clear go/no-go signals for SRE/product/eng/CS and (2) an adoption measurement plan that can be evaluated in weeks 0–12 post-launch.

Scope
-----
- Applies to hosted API rollout and Dedicated beta customers. Private/on-prem checklist is a subset (see linked runbook).
- Covers safety/perf signals, rollout cadence, instrumentation, adoption KPIs, and rollback criteria.

Quick timeline (high level)
-------------------------
- Week -6: Feature freeze on public API schema, begin smoke test matrix, instrumentation hooks merged to main.
- Week -4: Canary 2% internal traffic + 1 dedicated customer beta; begin daily signalboard standups.
- Week -2: 10% gradual rollout to low-risk traffic buckets; begin open adoption experiments.
- Week 0: 100% for new tier, staged migration window, support on-call ramp.
- Weeks 1–12: Adoption measurement windows, quality regressions gating promotional activities.

Signal definitions (operational)
--------------------------------
1) Latency & throughput
   - Primary: API P95 token latency (in ms). Measurement: prod APM + SDK metrics aggregated by model/route.
   - Go threshold: P95 <= 350ms for 95% of 12-hour windows during canary.
   - Soft alert: P95 > 300ms for 3 consecutive windows -> investigate.

2) Correctness & quality
   - Primary: Post-live regression rate on invariant eval set (weekly). Metric: fraction of prompts failing structural assertions.
   - Go threshold: no more than 1.5x baseline regression rate during canary.

3) Error & saturation
   - Primary: 5xx rate and backpressure events per 100k requests.
   - Go threshold: 5xx < 0.5% and queue-shed events = 0 during canary.

4) Cost-signal (unit economics)
   - Primary: tokens/second GPU cost delta vs baseline model. Target: <= +8% cost per token at parity latency.

Rollout cadence & gating (operational checklist)
-------------------------------------------------
- Pre-canary checklist (owners in parentheses):
  - Instrumentation validated for features/flags and prefix cache metrics (Liam Chen).
  - End-to-end smoke tests covering schema changes + streaming (QA lead).
  - Canary plan documented with traffic buckets and flagging method (feature-flagging team).
  - Emergency rollback runbook with SLA contacts (SRE oncall).

- Canary execution steps:
  - Step 0: Flip feature flag to internal 0.5% traffic for 24h; run smoke tests every 2h.
  - Step 1: If signals stable, increase to 2% and add one Dedicated beta customer for 72h.
  - Step 2: 10% for 48h if stable, run gated promotion for low-risk customers.
  - Step 3: Full rollout only after 72h at 10% and no gating triggers.

Canary gating triggers (immediate abort conditions)
---------------------------------------------------
- Any single 12-hour window where P95 > 500ms.
- Any 5xx spike > 1.5% sustained for 1 hour.
- Data corruption or schema failures observed in >0.1% of processed requests.
- Significant quality regression: >2x baseline invariant failure rate in a 24h window.

Adoption KPIs (measurement plan)
--------------------------------
We measure adoption across three lenses: product usage, customer value, and strategic distribution. Each KPI includes owner, query, target, and cadence.

- KPI: Daily Active Integrations (DAI)
  - Owner: Priya Nair
  - Query: Count of distinct API keys calling new /v2/batch endpoint in 24h.
  - Target: 150 DAI by week 4, 450 by week 12.
  - Cadence: daily; week-over-week growth % reported.

- KPI: Successful Batching Ratio (SBR)
  - Owner: Marisol Gomez
  - Query: fraction of requests served with batching enabled and latency <= target.
  - Target: SBR >= 60% at week 8 for eligible clients.
  - Cadence: daily, with breakdown by client tier.

- KPI: Feature Retention Rate (FRR)
  - Owner: Ethan Wallace
  - Query: % of integrations that made at least 3 calls/week by week 6 after first use.
  - Target: 45% retention at week 6.
  - Cadence: weekly cohorts (by signup date).

Instrumentation checklist (must be merged before -6)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Per-route token counters and P95/P50/P99 histograms exported to metrics backend (Prometheus/Datadog).
- Event logging for batching decisions (why a request was batched or not) with sampling 1% full traces for debugging.
- Canary-only tracing header support to isolate canary traffic.
- Business events: integration_created, batching_enabled, migration_completed mapped to analytics pipeline.
- Alerting: PagerDuty runbook for critical signals + Slack channel #launch-cadence alerts.

Customer success & comms plan
-----------------------------
- Beta cohort email templates (CS): onboarding checklist, known limitations, expected behavior and how to opt-out.
- Support playbook: triage matrix for latency vs quality incidents and escalation paths.
- Post-launch promotion gating: delay outbound newsletter until week 4 and only if quality signals stable.

Post-launch experiments (weeks 1–12)
------------------------------------
- Experiment A: Incentivized migration: small credits for Dedicated customers who switch to batching for 2 weeks.
- Experiment B: UI nudges in Console showing estimated cost savings per customer if batching enabled.
- Experiment C: A/B of two default batch size heuristics to measure SBR and latency tradeoffs.

Contingency & rollback playbook
--------------------------------
- Soft rollback: disable batching heuristics and revert to baseline serving path via feature flag.
- Hard rollback: circuit-break to previous model version; contact SRE lead + customer success for impacted customers.
- Customer communication template for both soft and hard rollback scenarios included in linked_artifacts.

Metrics ownership & reporting
-----------------------------
- Daily signalboard sync (15min): SRE, product, eng triage if any gating signals.
- Weekly deeper review: product-ops compiles adoption dashboard and sends to GTM and exec sponsors.
- Postmortem: Any canary abort requires a 48h postmortem and a remediation plan.

Open questions / outstanding actions
----------------------------------
- Need validation of P95 measurement on long-streaming sessions (assigned: Liam Chen).
- Confirm GA instrumentation for private deployments (assigned: Sofia Martinez).
- Finalize onboarding emails and migration incentives with growth (PR for templates: github PR in linked_artifacts).

Next steps (short)
------------------
- Merge instrumentation PRs and tag release candidate (RC) build: due 2025-11-10 (Liam)
- Run full canary smoke matrix internally at -7: assigned QA lead (Priya)
- Confirm Dedicated beta customer list and send invitations (Marisol)
- Schedule playbook dry-run with SRE + CS oncall (Sofia)

Notes to reviewers
------------------
- This doc is intentionally concise; the goal is a portable signalboard that can be copied for other product launches. Add comments inline for gaps.

Version history
---------------
- v0.1 2025-11-03: initial draft (Marisol)
- v0.2 2025-12-09: added KPI targets and experiments (Priya)
- v1.0 2026-02-28: updated thresholds after perf benching (Liam)
